description: Tests whether e_k is ADDITIVE over its two edges.  The cost is exactly separable once the forced run length l = S_top + S_bot is substituted into sum u^2; this measures whether the gain separates too, by comparing the exact excess of both edges together against the sum of each alone.  Every value is the exact O(L^2) excess in scaled integers, with the cost from the Lean identity staircase_two_mul_hookSum_sub.

checks.name: S1 the evaluator reproduces every reconstructed maximiser of PR #7323
checks.detail: 5 shapes, k = 8..35; max |diff| = 4.36e-22 against a DERIVED floor of 2.376e-21 — the recorded values are 22-digit renderings, so that is the comparison's resolution and not this arithmetic's.  Those values were themselves checked against the published heuristic excess, so this is a two-step agreement and the evaluator is not being calibrated against itself

checks.name: S2 the two edges are NOT additive — the residual is an interface count, not far field
checks.detail: max |E_both - E_top - E_bot| = 0.617 over 16 pairs at k = 40, against the far-field scale eps(4k) = 3.157e-15 — fourteen orders apart, so additivity is REFUTED and not marginally.  The COST does separate exactly (sum u^2 = top part + bottom part once the run's forced length l = S_top + S_bot is substituted), so the residual is entirely gain-side, and its size identifies it: the combined shape has ONE run with TWO interfaces where the two single-edge shapes have two runs with FOUR.  Combining saves an interface pair, which is an O(1) gain, not a far-field one.  It is not constant either (0.516 to 0.617 across these pairs) because a run's two interfaces still interact at eps(2*length)

checks.name: S3 the separable prediction understates the joint maximum, but picks the same argmax
checks.detail: max E_top + max E_bot = 1.797052992841246 against a jointly searched 2.414090644173904, short by 0.617038.  So e_inf is NOT max E_top + max E_bot.  What does survive is the argmax: the joint optimum is the same pair of profiles the two single-edge searches pick independently, so the two edges still choose their own shapes and only the VALUE fails to add

checks.name: S4 widening the profile bounds does not move either edge maximum
checks.detail: top (3, 2, 1, 1) -> (3, 2, 1, 1), bottom (1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1) -> (1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1); values unchanged.  Without this the two maxima would be bound artefacts and the sum would not be e_inf

checks.name: S5 max E_top = max E_bot exactly — one edge energy, seen twice
checks.detail: both 0.89852649642062312021, equal as scaled INTEGERS (difference exactly 0).  So there is one edge energy here, not two, and the exact equality of two independently-maximised searches is a check on the evaluator as much as an observation about the shapes.  CORRECTED 2026-09-13 (PR #7335): this detail used to add that the staircase is self-conjugate and the hook multiset a transpose invariant, 'so a top-edge deformation and its conjugate bottom-edge deformation carry the same excess; (3, 2, 1, 1) and (1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1) are that pair'.  The last clause is FALSE and was never checked — (3, 2, 1, 1) transposes to [4, 2, 1], which is not [1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1].  Transpose invariance remains the likely mechanism; the correspondence between these particular tuples is not identified.  The EQUALITY is measured and stands

verdict: REFUTED: e_k does not add over its two edges.  The COST does separate exactly, but the gain does not — E_both exceeds E_top + E_bot by ~0.6 at k = 40, fourteen orders above the far-field scale.  The size identifies the mechanism: one joint run has TWO interfaces where two single-edge runs have FOUR, so combining saves an interface pair.  The argmax does survive — the joint optimum is the pair each edge picks alone — so the two edges choose independently and only the value fails to add. Separately established: the number of extension rows is a SHAPE parameter and must be searched; fixing it at 3 gave 2.3684 at k = 40, which is below e_35 = 2.3764 and so impossible.  Best in class at k = 40: 2.414090644173904.
